title: Fifteen India-Pakistan finals, one shared trophy: the complete record of the fiercest summit rivalry
excerpt: From Miandad's last-ball six in Sharjah to India's Asia Cup triumph in Dubai, here is every India-Pakistan final across cricket and hockey — a ledger that stands level at seven wins apiece.
body:
• India and Pakistan have met in 15 tournament finals across cricket and hockey, and the outright ledger stands level: seven wins each, with one shared hockey title.
  • In cricket's 10 finals, Pakistan leads 6-4 — but India's four wins include the 2007 T20 World Cup and the 2025 Asia Cup, their first final victory over Pakistan in 18 years.
  • In hockey's five finals, India leads 3-1, from the 4-2 Asia Cup triumph in Kuala Lumpur in 2003 to the rain-shared 2018 Asian Champions Trophy.
  • The rivalry's next final is days away: India meets Pakistan in the Asian Games 2026 men's T20 cricket gold-medal match on October 3.

When India chased down Pakistan's 146 in the Asia Cup final in Dubai last September — sealing a ninth Asia Cup title — it was the latest chapter in a ledger 40 years in the making. Across cricket and hockey, India and Pakistan have now contested 15 tournament finals. The count: India seven, Pakistan seven, one shared. Nobody leads.

Cricket: ten finals, four decades of drama

It began in Melbourne in March 1985, at the Benson & Hedges World Championship of Cricket. Kapil Dev's India bowled Pakistan out for 176 before Kris Srikkanth's 67 and Ravi Shastri's unbeaten half-century carried India home by eight wickets. Shastri drove away in an Audi 100 as Champion of Champions — India's first final win over Pakistan.

Fourteen months later came the rivalry's most replayed moment. In the 1986 Austral-Asia Cup final in Sharjah, Pakistan needed four off the final ball with one wicket standing; Javed Miandad, unbeaten on 116, launched Chetan Sharma for six. Sharjah became Pakistan's fortress: they beat India in finals there again in 1991, when 19-year-old Aaqib Javed's 7/37 routed India by 72 runs in the Wills Trophy, and in 1994, when Aamer Sohail's all-round show secured a 39-run win after Pakistan posted 250.

India's answer came in Dhaka in January 1998. The Independence Cup final was a rare best-of-three series, and the decider was a classic: after Saeed Anwar's 140 and Ijaz Ahmed's 117 lifted Pakistan to 314, Sourav Ganguly's 124 and Robin Singh's 82 kept India in the chase before Hrishikesh Kanitkar's last-over boundary sealed a 2-1 series win.

Pakistan struck back in the 1999 Pepsi Cup final in Bangalore — Inzamam-ul-Haq's 91 and Azhar Mahmood's 5/38 skittling India for 169 — and in the 2008 Kitply Cup final in Dhaka, where Pakistan defended 315 for a 25-run win.

But India's wins came on the biggest stages. In Johannesburg in September 2007, Gautam Gambhir's 75 lifted India to 157/5 in the first T20 World Cup final; Misbah-ul-Haq's attempted scoop off Joginder Sharma found Sreesanth at fine leg with six needed off four balls, and India won by five runs — their first world title in 24 years. In London in June 2017 the script flipped: Fakhar Zaman's 114 powered Pakistan to 338/4, Mohammad Amir destroyed India's top order, and Pakistan won by 180 runs, their biggest margin over India in an ICC final.

Then Dubai, September 2025. Pakistan collapsed from 113/1 to 146 all out — Kuldeep Yadav took 4/30 on his way to 17 wickets for the tournament — and India chased it down for their ninth Asia Cup crown. It ended an 18-year wait for a final win over Pakistan. In cricket finals: Pakistan leads 6-4.

Hockey: India's turf

On the hockey field the record reverses. In Kuala Lumpur in September 2003, Dhanraj Pillay's India beat Pakistan 4-2 in the Asia Cup final — early strikes, then Ignace Tirkey and Prabhjot Singh in the final two minutes — for India's first Asia Cup title.

The Asian Champions Trophy has since become the rivalry's hockey home: India won the inaugural 2011 final in Ordos on a shootout, Pakistan answered 5-4 in Doha in 2012, India took Kuantan 2016 by 3-2, and the 2018 final in Muscat was abandoned to rain and shared. Across hockey's five finals: India three, Pakistan one, one shared.

What the ledger says

The pattern of eras is striking: Pakistan dominated the Sharjah years of the late 1980s and 1990s, winning four of five cricket finals in that stretch. India's wins cluster on the biggest platforms — a World Championship in 1985, a World T20 in 2007, an Asia Cup in 2025 — while Pakistan owns the 2017 Champions Trophy and the tri-nation trophies. In overall T20 internationals India dominates the rivalry at an 81.25% win rate, per Cricbuzz, but in finals — where one innings decides everything — it is dead even.

Diaspora angle

For the diaspora, these finals have always been played on home turf wherever they land: Melbourne in 1985 was an Indian crowd's coronation, Sharjah in the 1990s a Pakistani stronghold, Dubai in 2025 split down the middle. Neutral venues turn India-Pakistan finals into the diaspora's biggest shared ritual — and the next one is in Aichi-Nagoya.

What's next

The 16th final arrives on October 3, when defending champions India meet Pakistan in the Asian Games 2026 men's T20 gold-medal match at 10:00 AM IST. A win gives India their fifth cricket final victory and, for the first time, the outright lead in the finals ledger.
image_caption: India's players celebrate beating Pakistan in the Asia Cup final in Dubai. The September 2025 win was India's first tournament-final victory over Pakistan in 18 years.
nri_angle: India-Pakistan finals at neutral venues like Melbourne, Sharjah and Dubai are the diaspora's biggest shared sporting ritual, and the October 3 Asian Games gold-medal match gives overseas fans the 16th chapter at a fan-friendly hour.
